deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on 'topologie modérée' (tame topology), 1974. On the previous page Grothendieck works in a piecewise-linear, piecewise-algebraic or piecewise-analytic setting. In modern terms this is semialgebraic, subanalytic or o-minimal-like. He defines partitions of spaces into 'feuilles' (leaves, i.e. strata).

The previous page sets up three notions:
- An *admissible* system of partitions for a diagram of spaces X = (X_i)_{i in I}.
- An *equisingular* system: the induced diagram of maps between 'closed leaves' \bar F_{i,alpha} -> \bar F_{j,beta} is locally topologically trivial along every leaf of every X_i.
- A *privileged* system: equisingular, and in addition the 'closures of leaves' are manifolds. These are presumably the abstract closed leaves \bar F, i.e. manifolds with boundary or corners.

Conjecture 1 there says every space has a privileged partition, and among them a coarsest one, called 'canonical'.

This page extends the problem in three ways.
1. Grothendieck notes that Conjecture 1 is insufficient for applications. One also needs privileged admissible partitions that:
   - refine a given partition;
   - make finitely many given closed subsets X_i of X unions of leaves, with the induced filtration privileged;
   - are compatible with a given map X -> Y, partitioning source and target simultaneously.
2. He unifies all these cases in Conjecture 2. Let I be a finite ordered set and (X_i)_{i in I} an I-diagram of tame spaces whose transition maps X_i -> X_j are proper. Then privileged systems of partitions of the diagram exist, and there is a coarsest one, again 'canonical'. Closed subspaces correspond to diagrams of closed inclusions (proper), a map to the poset {0<1}, a given partition to its filtration by closed unions of strata.
3. Remark, with proof continued on the next page. Let the partition of the diagram be admissible, f: X_i -> X_j proper, F a leaf of X_i mapping into a leaf S (written Phi, then 𝓛, then 𝒮 on the next page) of X_j.
   - Then f(F) = S, not merely an open subset of S. f(F) is open by equisingularity, and closed in S by properness, since S \ f(F) is covered by images of smaller leaves in \bar F ∩ f^{-1}(S). As S is connected, f(F) = S.
   - Since F is locally trivially fibred over the open set f(F), it is locally trivial over all of S. Better, f^{-1}(S) with its induced partition is a locally trivial stratified bundle over S.
   - Since F and S are manifolds, the fibres are manifolds.
   This is the stratified Ehresmann/Thom-isotopy picture: a proper stratified map is a stratified locally trivial fibration over each target stratum.

The next page then proposes a recursive construction of the canonical partition of a proper map f: X -> Y with Y compact. Take the largest open U of Y that is nonsingular and over which f is locally trivial. Prove Y \ U is a nowhere-dense tame subspace of lower dimension, take connected components of U as leaves, and recurse. It also refers to an earlier description, in the 'question relative à A'Campo', of the canonical partition of a space via 'immobile' points.

Purpose: foundations for a tame, stratified topology, with canonical stratifications functorial for proper maps and diagrams. This is a precursor of the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse d'un programme (1984).
errors: The condition 'closures of leaves are manifolds' cannot literally mean topological closures in X. For a nodal curve, the closure of the open stratum is the whole singular curve. It must refer to abstract 'closed leaves' (\bar F, likely manifolds with boundary or corners obtained by cutting out tubular neighbourhoods), defined on earlier pages. As stated on these pages the condition is ambiguous.

Existence of a coarsest privileged partition is far from automatic. The supremum of two equisingular partitions need not be equisingular, and the 'closed leaves are manifolds' requirement may be destroyed by coarsening. Conjecture 2 is a genuine conjecture, and for maps a coarsest topologically trivial stratification is delicate.

Notation slip: the target leaf is called Phi and then 𝓛 (𝒮 on the next page). The argument in the Remark is otherwise correct, given properness and connectedness of S. Openness of f(F) needs the equisingularity (local triviality) hypothesis, which he invokes on the next page.
'propre' is struck in the remark but properness is used in the proof (closedness of the image); it is presumably assumed from the diagram hypothesis.

ideas.what: Coarsest ('canonical') equisingular/privileged stratification of a tame space
ideas.modern_name: Canonical/minimal stratification: minimal Whitney stratification; intrinsic stratification of polyhedra by local homeomorphism type
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney (1965), Mather (1970), Teissier (1982) for minimal Whitney; Akin (1969) and others for intrinsic PL stratifications
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 on tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures, discusses such questions in general terms

ideas.what: Privileged partitions refining a given partition, adapted to finitely many closed subsets with privileged induced filtration
ideas.modern_name: Stratifications compatible with a finite family of subsets (o-minimal cell decomposition / Whitney stratification compatible with given definable sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Łojasiewicz, Hironaka (1973–75), van den Dries (o-minimal setting)

ideas.what: Simultaneous canonical stratification of a finite poset-indexed diagram of proper tame maps (Conjecture 2)
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of maps/diagrams (Thom–Mather stratified maps, Hardt triviality); canonical stratification of diagrams
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970–73), Hardt (1980) for existence for maps; Gibson–Wirthmüller–du Plessis–Looijenga (1976) for diagrams of maps in stability theory

ideas.what: Proper equisingular stratified map sends each leaf onto a whole target leaf and is a locally trivial stratified bundle over it, with manifold fibres
ideas.modern_name: Thom's first isotopy lemma / stratified Ehresmann theorem

missed.claim: Conjecture 2: for any finite-poset-indexed diagram of proper tame maps there exist privileged (equisingular, with manifold closed leaves) partitions, and a coarsest canonical one. Existence of stratifications of maps is known (Hardt, Verdier, Thom–Mather). The existence of a coarsest topologically equisingular one for arbitrary finite diagrams of proper maps, with the extra 'closed leaves are manifolds' condition, is not, as far as I know, a standard settled result.
missed.quote: il existe des partitions privilégiées dans ce diagramme, et il y a parmi elles une moins fine (appelée comme de juste "canonique")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Canonical, functorial stratifications of diagrams would make the o-minimal/tame stratified setting strictly functorial. This is relevant to constructible sheaves, exit-path ∞-categories and stratified homotopy theory, where functoriality in proper maps and diagrams is wanted.

missed.claim: Grothendieck packages refinement, adaptation to closed subsets, and compatibility with maps into one statement about diagrams indexed by finite posets. This categorical reformulation of stratification theory is not the standard way the literature organises these results.
missed.quote: Tous ces cas semblent contenus par l'énoncé conjectural suivant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates treating stratifications as functors on posets, as in modern stratified spaces over posets (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). It suggests a canonical-stratification functor on diagrams.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is mostly in line with Thom–Mather–Whitney stratification theory and the later Esquisse programme. The diagram-indexed canonical stratification conjecture is a notable unpublished formulation, but its components (existence for maps, minimal stratifications) were developed independently.
